title: Rabbi Levi bar Chiyya
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Berakhot 64a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.64a.11) he says: “One who leaves the synagogue, enters the study house and studies Torah merits receiving the Divine Presence,” as in “They go from strength,” etc. The saying also appears at [the end of Moed Katan](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.29a.5) with the unqualified Rabbi Levi, but Dikdukei Soferim reads Rabbi Levi bar Chiyyata.[^1]
And in [Bereshit Rabbah 13:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.13.3): Rabbi Levi bar Ḥiyya said, And the three of them are from three letters, etc.
And in [Shemot Rabbah 23:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Shemot_Rabbah.23.3), a fine parable from him.
And likewise a homily from him is found in [Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Shir_HaShirim_Rabbah.1.12.1).[^2]

notes.text: Berakhot gives Rabbi Levi bar Chiyya. The parallel teaching in Moed Katan gives Rabbi Levi without a patronymic. Hyman reports bar Chiyyata from Dikdukei Soferim. Heilprin has separate notices for [bar Chiyya](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2349&lang=en) and [bar Chiyyata](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2348&lang=en).
The linked midrashim all give the name as Levi bar Chia (חיא). The passages discuss three words of three letters, a parable about making amends through the same word, and the wood of the Tabernacle.
